A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HypER research and contain the main text and Appendices A–J. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, results, figures, tables, and prompts without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original chain-validation experiments, hypothesis-generation evaluations, expert ratings, and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and Appendices D–I.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds teacher–expert disagreement results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The chain construction, negative sampling, multitask fine-tuning, and generation procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D's preference for relevance score 2 with fallback to score 1 already appears in v1 Section 3; the expanded model identifiers do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RCT/PubMed-derived medical data, four medical subdisciplines, and valid/easy-negative/hard-negative chain scenarios. Evaluation outside medicine is proposed as future work, not newly performed.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Table 2 and Appendix I are retained, including the abstract-only Phi-3 comparison. Appendix I.1 changes an inconsistent prose reference from GPT-4 to GPT-4o, which Table 8 already identifies in both versions; this is not a baseline replacement.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a targeted diagnostic criterion: cases where the teacher assigns relevance score 2 but an expert assigns 0, assessed separately for each expert. Existing splits, training settings, main evaluation metrics, and stated sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an error analysis asking whether moderate overall teacher–expert agreement conceals clearly irrelevant papers among highly rated candidates. The existing chain-length analysis, human–LLM comparisons, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 20-seed teacher assessment, agreement statistics, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and human–LLM correlations. The added disagreement percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimates or establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Appendix D newly reports score-2 versus score-0 disagreement percentages of 7.8%, 2.0%, and 0% for the three experts. Existing classification, groundedness, hypothesis-rating, and chain-length results retain their reported values.

T1.justification: The literature-graph and reasoning-chain definitions, task formulations, and mathematical expressions are retained. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the assertion that the framework is generalizable beyond medicine to potential applicability requiring validation in additional domains. The central contributions and abstract/conclusion performance claims otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly argues that relevance subjectivity makes moderate agreement expected and interprets the reported severe-disagreement percentages as supporting the teacher's practical suitability. The introduction also explicitly qualifies applicability beyond the evaluated medical domain.

D1.justification: Section 4 specifies meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and MistralLite's load_in_4bit: true flag; Appendix D explicitly identifies the instruction-tuned teacher. These refine existing documentation: v1 already described instruction-tuned baselines and labeled Mistral as 4-bit. Prompts, LoRA settings, hardware, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and comparisons with prior research in Section 6 and Appendix A remain unchanged. The research-positioning table and distinctions from SCIMON and ResearchAgent are retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands model labels, corrects the GPT-4o description and institutional affiliation, adds funding acknowledgments, and makes localized prose additions. The overall section sequence and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays undergo limited resizing and relocation: Table 3 changes column on page 7, Table 5 moves across columns, and Table 9 moves from page 16 to page 17. The figures and table structures are retained without new visualizations.

improvement.justification: v2 improves claim calibration by treating nonmedical generalization as unvalidated, clarifies model configurations, and adds targeted evidence about teacher-label quality in Appendix D. These are useful but limited gains: the central experimental validation is unchanged, and the new disagreement percentages lack explicit denominators and uncertainty estimates.
